summary: Recent headlines highlight ongoing congressional constraints on D.C.'s local governance, from naming authority over federal buildings to budget autonomy, alongside renewed advocacy for statehood. A senator has committed to prioritizing D.C. statehood, while advocates reference federal intervention in the District's affairs as evidence that statehood is urgently needed. Without statehood, D.C. cannot spend its own local tax revenue until Congress approves its budget, and Congress retains veto power over D.C.'s local laws and policies.
